html:
Borikén was the Taino name for Puerto Rico. Its people were farmers who grew cassava in mounded fields, fished, and lived in villages under caciques. They played a ball game in stone-lined courts; the site of Caguana still shows them.

Columbus passed the island in 1493. In 1508 Juan Ponce de León began Spanish settlement, and the Taino were forced to work for settlers in gold washing and farming. In 1511 the caciques led by Agüeybaná II rose against the Spanish and were crushed. Disease and forced labour then cut their numbers drastically. Taino words and genes live on in Puerto Rico, and many Puerto Ricans claim Taino ancestry today. Its neighbour was the island of Hispaniola.
